statement: Every behaviour-changing desired-replication-factor read in the inventoried consumer set resolves through the single replication-target policy authority and through nothing else: no consumer derives a replication target from an identity count, applies a local fallback default, or reinterprets an undeclared policy as a usable number; the known move-planner placement-target divergence is witnessed and recorded in the inventory without behaviour change; and the self-hosted message group's declared policy is proved convergible by replica recovery to its declared factor. The inventory claim is sealed: eleven behaviour-changing consumers on canonical persisted-policy semantics plus one divergent placement-target consumer whose repair is transferred to S6b.

constraints.statement: If this Quest changes source code, spawn a subagent verifier before audit and git handoff, then record a Solver finding with evidence subagent:<id>.

Exactly one module is the AUTHORITY that behaviour-changing desired-RF readers resolve through: every inventoried consumer obtains its replication target by calling the replication-target authority on the persisted policy row, and no inventoried consumer reads replica_count or replicaCount policy columns directly, counts identities as a target, or applies a local || or ?? fallback default to the resolved factor.

Where the authority decodes UNDECLARED, the consumer takes an explicit undeclared path - it skips the action and surfaces a diagnostic - and never substitutes a config minimum, schema default, or identity count. Only the formation barrier may use a bootstrap expected RF, and only to stay blocked, never to release or to act.

The move-planner placement-target divergence (policy.targetReplicaCount || policy.replicaCount || NUM.THREE via the table-policy fallback) is witnessed and recorded in the inventory; its behaviour is NOT changed by this Quest. Repair is transferred to S6b, which must route the planner target to the same authoritative persisted policy before S4 becomes authoritative.

The self-hosted message group's declared policy really is the MESSAGE_GROUPS schema declaration (RF 3): replica recovery must be capable of converging a one-replica self-hosted group to the declared factor once enough eligible distinct nodes exist, witnessed deterministically. Restoring the observed identity count of 1 into any policy field is forbidden.

CLI views, navigation, and admin diagnostics that render replica_count are display-only observers: they are inventoried as non-behaviour-changing and left unchanged; the service plane (service-descriptor replicaCount, SD_COL.REPLICA_COUNT, join-admission observed-count projection) stays in service-plane-replication-authority-inventory and is not silently absorbed here.

Proof is a deterministic raw node:test witness with one anchored scenario per receipt, red on HEAD and green after for every behaviour-changing routing, with a mutation matrix in which every reintroduced local fallback, identity-count target, or authority bypass reds at least one named receipt.
